hypotheses.statement: solang rejects the bare Solidity builtin `ecrecover(hash, v, r, s)` at compile time with 'unknown function or type ecrecover', while solc accepts it; this is a pure compile-time asymmetry, so no runtime ecrecover semantics (v=27/28 vs 0/1, Substrate account recovery) can be probed until solang-side syntax/availability is resolved.

evidence.note: solc compiled fine; solang failed with 'unknown function or type ecrecover' on both ecrecover call sites — all hash-builtin runtime results were unobservable.

hypotheses.next_probe: Compile-and-run a probe identical to this one but with the ecrecover calls removed (only keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 over abi.encodePacked vs abi.encode), to verify the three hash builtins compile under solang and match solc bit-for-bit; separately, try `ecrecover` via the `signature` form documented for solang (or an ECDSA recovery library) to determine if any solang-side ecrecover path exists.

hypotheses.statement: Hypothesis: solang supports keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 builtins (they are not implicated in the compile error), so a hash-only probe should compile under both toolchains and produce identical storage values — refuted only if solang rejects one of them or a value mismatch appears.

evidence.note: The solang error named only ecrecover (lines 18-19); hash builtin call sites at lines 13-16 drew no error, suggesting they parse under solang but their runtime behavior is untested.

Hash-only probe compiled and ran under both toolchains, but all six storage values / return values diverged: solang-side keccak256, sha256, and ripemd160 digests all differ from EVM solc outputs for the same inputs. The 'hash builtins match bit-for-bit' prediction is falsified.

hypotheses.next_probe: crypto-hash-only probe: keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 over abi.encodePacked(uint8,uint16,uint64,uint256) and abi.encode of the same, queried from storage, no ecrecover anywhere.

hypotheses.statement: solang's keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 digests diverge from EVM because solang's abi.encode/abi.encodePacked feed the hash non-canonical, tightly packed bytes (encodedLen = 43 = packed length, h5 confirmed), not because the hash primitives are wrong; explanation (b) (wrong primitive over identical bytes) is now disfavored but not fully refuted — it survives only if a constant-input, encoding-free hash (keccak256 of a fixed bytes literal) still mismatches the known EVM answer.

evidence.note: encodedKeccak differs: EVM 0x4cf8beb6...e1f6 vs polkadot 0x3ed8459b...a02d. abi.encode(uint8,uint16,uint64,uint256) should be canonical 128-byte padding on both chains, so a correct keccak256 over identical bytes should match; mismatch implies either a non-keccak hash primitive on the solang side or a non-standard abi.encode. Same pattern for sha256 (0x46b8c5e6... vs 0xc571f7b8...) and ripemd160 (0x51de5651... vs 0x7933883e...).

All six digests diverge from EVM as before, but every polkadot digest differs from the previous probe's polkadot digests (e.g. encodedKeccak 0x3ed8459b... -> 0x37346b7d...), proving the hash functions respond to inputs rather than emitting constants. Since packed==encode on solang (h4 confirmed), the EVM-vs-solang gap must come from either the encoding bytes or the hash primitive, not from packing.

For mixed dynamic args (170,'hi',0x1234), packedKeccak is bit-identical across chains (0x51a70842... on both EVM and polkadot) and packedSha is bit-identical (0x768f2543... on both). Since the packed bytes are the same input on both sides, identical digests prove solang's keccak256 and sha256 primitives are correct; simultaneously, encodedKeccak (0xd93584a9... vs 0x0987b47c...) and encodedSha (0xc35682c6... vs 0x80043acc...) diverge, so the digest gaps live entirely in abi.encode's non-canonical bytes. Explanation (b) (wrong hash primitive) is refuted for keccak256/sha256; the encoding explanation (a) is confirmed.

hypotheses.next_probe: Hash a compile-time constant with no ABI encoding at all: store keccak256(hex'1234') (or keccak256 of a fixed bytes literal constant) and compare against the known EVM value 0x56570de287d73cd1cb6092bb8fbf61714b954181e5f0bf1e3f09e12576c46a5c (keccak256(0x1234)). If it matches, solang's keccak256 is correct and the divergence lives in abi.encode/abi.encodePacked; if it differs, the hash primitive itself is wrong.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked ignores packing and produces the same bytes as abi.encode (32-byte-slot padding), because on the polkadot side the packed and encoded digests were identical for all three hash functions (packedKeccak == encodedKeccak, packedSha == encodedSha, packedRipemd == encodedRipemd), whereas EVM produced distinct digests for the two encodings.

evidence.note: On polkadot, packedKeccak == encodedKeccak == 0x3ed8459b..., packedSha == encodedSha == 0xc571f7b8..., packedRipemd == encodedRipemd == 0x7933883e..., strongly implying abi.encodePacked(a,b,c,d) yields the same 128 padded bytes as abi.encode(a,b,c,d) under solang. Caveat: if the hash divergence (h3) turns out to be input-independent (e.g., wrong primitive), identical outputs would be expected even with correct packing, so this needs isolation.

With a different arg set (0, 48879, 81985529216486895, 2e19), polkadot again shows packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x37346b7d..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xd7137cff..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x0ba1282a..., while EVM produces distinct digests for the two encodings. Critically, the polkadot digests changed from the previous probe's values, so the hash is input-dependent; identical digests for packed vs encode over two independent input sets therefore imply identical input bytes, i.e. abi.encodePacked does not pack under solang.

hypotheses.next_probe: Direct length probe: expose a view function returning abi.encodePacked(a,b,c,d).length and abi.encode(a,b,c,d).length. EVM returns 17 and 128; if solang returns 128/128 it confirms packed==encode (encodePacked bug); if it returns 17/128 the packing is correct and the divergence is purely in the hash/encode primitives.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode(uint8,uint16,uint64,uint256) does not emit the canonical 128-byte Solidity encoding (32-byte slot padding per argument); its encoded bytes differ from EVM's, which alone would explain why keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 digests diverge even if solang's hash primitives are individually correct. Evidence: solang's encodedKeccak for the (170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) arg set is 0x3ed8459b... while EVM's is 0x4cf8beb6... despite abi.encode being chain-independent canonical padding; and solang's digests are fully deterministic and input-dependent (0x3ed8459b... for a=170 vs 0x41b8ea53... for a=128, with all other args identical), so the gap is a systematic encoding/primitive difference, not nondeterminism.

evidence.note: Two set() calls varying only a (170 then 128): all polkadot digests changed (packedKeccak 0x3ed8459b... -> 0x41b8ea53...) and the a=170 polkadot values exactly reproduce the original probe's polkadot values (0x3ed8459b...), proving both chains are deterministic and the solang digests for a previously seen input are stable. Since abi.encode of this static tuple must be byte-identical on any correct implementation, the persistent solang/EVM digest gap under determinism points at either non-canonical abi.encode bytes or wrong hash primitives; the determinism datum rules out flakiness as an explanation.

encodedLen(170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) returns 128 on EVM but 43 on polkadot. 43 = 1+2+8+32 is exactly the packed length of the four arguments, proving solang's abi.encode(uint8,uint16,uint64,uint256) emits tightly packed bytes with no 32-byte slot padding. Since identical digests for packed vs encode (h4) now have a direct length corroboration, the persistent keccak256/sha256/ripemd160 digest divergence is fully explained by non-canonical abi.encode input bytes; no wrong-hash-primitive hypothesis is needed for those probes.

hypotheses.next_probe: Expose abi.encode(a,b,c,d) and abi.encodePacked(a,b,c,d) lengths via a view function (EVM expects 128 and 17), and additionally return the raw abi.encode bytes for a fixed arg set to compare against the known 128-byte EVM canonical encoding byte-for-byte.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode for DYNAMIC types (string, bytes) is broken in a way that is not merely 'packed': abi.encode(170,'hi',0x1234) yields 7 bytes on polkadot vs 224 on EVM, while abi.encodePacked yields the same value on both chains (packedLenStr steps matched, EVM packed = 1+2+2 = 5). The 7-byte output is neither the canonical 224-byte encoding nor the 5-byte packed encoding, so solang's encoder invents a third, unspecified layout for dynamic arguments (7 = 1+2+4 hints at a 4-byte length prefix for the bytes argument or similar ad-hoc framing).

evidence.note: Predictions verified via dual-hash evidence: abi.encodePacked(170,'hi',0x1234) produces byte-identical output on both chains (two independent hash functions agree bit-for-bit: keccak 0x51a70842..., sha256 0x768f2543...), while abi.encode(170,'hi',0x1234) produces different bytes (keccak 0xd93584a9... vs 0x0987b47c...; sha256 0xc35682c6... vs 0x80043acc...). Combined with h3's now-established hash correctness, solang's abi.encode for dynamic types is confirmed broken in a way that is not merely 'packed', consistent with the previously observed 7-byte vs 224-byte length asymmetry.

hypotheses.next_probe: Return raw bytes: expose abi.encode(170,'hi',0x1234) and abi.encodePacked(170,'hi',0x1234) as `returns (bytes memory)` view functions on both chains and diff the hex; also test abi.encode of a single string and single bytes to map the per-type framing rule (e.g. whether a length prefix is 2 or 4 bytes).

hypotheses.statement: solang's keccak256 and sha256 hash primitives are bit-for-bit correct relative to EVM: when both chains hash provably identical bytes (abi.encodePacked over mixed dynamic types), the digests match exactly on both functions. Therefore all keccak256/sha256 digest divergences observed in this campaign are attributable to the ABI encoder layer (abi.encode non-canonical, abi.encodePacked static-type padding per h4/h5), not to the crypto implementations; ripemd160 is predicted to be correct as well but is not yet directly validated on matching bytes.

evidence.note: packedKeccak 0x51a70842fcacfed5f1d62e4528b66fbb07be65fd1a760f3f037d5575cb9a1548 and packedSha 0x768f25430a3de810458ea643baebfb2db2dcfac165c47185829646977f3d4880 are identical on EVM and polkadot for the same (uint8,string,bytes) input, while the encoded variants diverge — two independent hash functions agreeing across chains is strong evidence of correct primitives.

For an all-max-values tuple (255, 65535, 2^64-1, 2^256-1), packedRipemd is bit-identical across chains (0x2ad239455b4fc1bad5d7807a2158bdf90dc0b913 on both EVM and polkadot), joining packedKeccak (0x7cfb035b...) and packedSha (0x19462e5b...) which also matched exactly. All three hash primitives are now validated as correct over provably identical packed bytes; ripemd160 is exonerated and the entire crypto layer is confirmed sound for this builtin set.

hypotheses.next_probe: Rerun this exact mixed-types probe adding ripemd160(abi.encodePacked(a,b,c)) storage/return: if the packed ripemd160 digest matches across chains (prediction: yes), ripemd160 correctness is confirmed and the crypto layer is fully exonerated for all three builtins.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked has a static/dynamic asymmetry: for all-static multi-integer tuples it ignores packing and emits 32-byte-slot-padded bytes identical to its abi.encode (h4/h5, 128 vs 17 bytes on EVM), but for tuples containing dynamic types (string/bytes) it performs correct tight packing byte-identical to EVM (this probe). The encoder switches to correct packed layout exactly when dynamic arguments are present.

evidence.note: Mixed dynamic packed digests match EVM exactly, in contrast to the all-static probe where packedKeccak==encodedKeccak on polkadot (0x3ed8459b...) but diverged from EVM's true 17-byte-packed digest. The only structural difference between the probes is the presence of dynamic types, implicating a packing-path split in solang's encoder.

Step 0 (255,65535,2^64-1,2^256-1,'x') behaved as h8 predicted: packedKeccak (0xfcdcfcfe...) and packedSha (0x1ca4706b...) are bit-identical across chains, only encodedKeccak/encodedSha diverge. But step 1 (1,2,3,4,'') broke the rule: packedKeccak diverged (EVM 0x6387eff5... vs polkadot 0x56669b11...) and packedSha diverged (0x487f9503... vs 0xd2a7182d...), so the presence of a dynamic arg does not reliably trigger correct packing — an empty string corrupts the packed encoding on solang. h8's clean static/dynamic split is falsified.

hypotheses.next_probe: Boundary probe: measure abi.encodePacked(uint8,uint16,string).length and abi.encodePacked(uint256,uint256).length on both chains (EVM expects 1+2+2=5... actually 1+2+len('x')=4, and 64). Vary which argument position the dynamic type occupies (first/last) to map whether the presence of any dynamic arg triggers correct packing for the whole tuple or only for the dynamic tail.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked for all-static integer tuples is bit-for-bit correct relative to EVM even at type-maximum boundary values (255, 65535, 2^64-1, 2^256-1): all three packed digests (keccak256, sha256, ripemd160) match EVM exactly, ruling out sign-extension, truncation, or width bugs in solang's packed integer encoder at bit boundaries. The sole remaining solang anomaly for all-static tuples is the abi.encode==abi.encodePacked collapse (encodedKeccak == packedKeccak == 0x7cfb035b... on polkadot vs EVM's distinct canonical-128-byte digest 0x6e659349...).

evidence.note: At all-max args, polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x7cfb035b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x19462e5b..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x2ad23945..., while EVM produced six distinct values with packed digests exactly matching polkadot's packed side. This simultaneously re-confirms the packed==encode collapse at extremes and proves the packed path has no boundary-value bug.

Step 0 (all-max args) exactly reproduces the prior boundary probe: polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x7cfb035b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x19462e5b..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x2ad23945..., while EVM's six digests are distinct and its packed side matches polkadot's exactly. Step 1 (all-zero args) adds a second extreme: polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xdafb08ad..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x859732b9..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0xd93a7bc1..., again with EVM's packed digests matching polkadot bit-for-bit and only encoded diverging. Packed integer encoding is therefore correct at both value extremes (no zero special-casing, no boundary truncation), and the packed==encode collapse is not an artifact of large values.

hypotheses.next_probe: Cross the static/dynamic boundary in one tuple: abi.encodePacked(uint8 a, uint16 b, uint64 c, uint256 d, string s) with s='x' at max integer values — if the packed digest diverges from EVM, the presence of a dynamic arg corrupts even the static head of packing (refuting h8's clean split); if it matches, h8's 'dynamic arg triggers correct packing' rule is confirmed at boundaries.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode==abi.encodePacked collapse for all-static tuples is value-independent: it holds at all-max, all-zero, and intermediate arg sets, so solang's abi.encode never emits canonical 32-byte-slot padding for any all-static integer tuple. The collapse is hypothesized to extend to all static types (address, bool, bytesNN), meaning solang's abi.encode is systematically non-canonical for every argument list lacking dynamic types; the sole observed exception to wrong-packing is abi.encodePacked with dynamic types present (h8), which packs correctly.

evidence.note: Two independent extreme value sets (all-max and all-zero) both show polkadot encoded==packed while EVM keeps them distinct, so the collapse is a structural property of solang's encoder for static tuples, not a value-dependent quirk. All six polkadot packed digests across both steps match EVM's packed digests exactly, so the packed path is correct in both cases and the encoded path inherits it.

Two more intermediate value sets confirm the collapse is fully value-independent: step 0 (128,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) gives polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x41b8ea53... (exactly reproducing the p2 probe's a=128 polkadot value, re-confirming determinism), and step 1 (170,0,...) gives packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xd6e3246d..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xef508b2a..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x32ffae15..., while EVM keeps all six digests distinct. An interior zero (b=0) does not break the collapse, so it is a structural property of solang's static-tuple encoder, not value-dependent special-casing. The collapse for all-static integer tuples is now established across four independent arg sets (all-max, all-zero, two intermediates).

hypotheses.next_probe: Static non-integer probe: abi.encodePacked(address,bool,bytes4) and abi.encode(address,bool,bool) digests/lengths on both chains (EVM encode lengths 96 and 96; packed lengths 25 and 2). If solang's encode matches packed here too, the collapse generalizes to all static types; if encode is canonical for non-integer statics, the collapse is integer-tuple-specific.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked matches EVM bit-for-bit when the dynamic string argument is non-empty ('x' at max integer values, both keccak256 and sha256 digests identical across chains) but diverges when the string is empty (''), even with a tiny static head (1,2,3,4). Hypothesis: solang encodes an empty string in packed mode differently from EVM — e.g., omitting the length prefix entirely, emitting a 4-byte instead of 2-byte (or vice versa) length word, or dropping the empty dynamic tail while EVM appends a 0x0000 length — so the divergence is specific to zero-length dynamic values rather than a general dynamic-type packing failure (h8's non-empty 'hi' and 'x' cases both matched).

evidence.note: Within one probe both behaviors were observed: step 0 ('x') gave bit-identical packed digests on both chains for two independent hash functions, while step 1 ('') gave four distinct packed/encoded digests. Since h7 established the hash primitives are correct, the step-1 packed divergence must come from different packed bytes for the empty-string case on solang.

Predicted divergence for empty-string packed encoding did not materialize: emptyPackedLen, oneCharPackedLen, emptyAloneLen, and all three keccak256 digests (empty-packed, one-char-packed, empty-alone) are identical across solc/EVM and solang/polkadot. Solang frames an empty string in abi.encodePacked exactly like EVM (zero bytes appended, since packed strings carry no length prefix), so the p2-dyn-tail step-1 divergence is not a general empty-string rule.

hypotheses.next_probe: Length probe: expose a view returning abi.encodePacked(1,2,3,4,'').length and abi.encodePacked(1,2,3,4,'x').length (EVM expects 8+2=10 and 8+3=11: 1+2+8+32+len). If solang returns e.g. 8 or 12 for the empty case, the exact framing difference is pinned down; also compare abi.encodePacked('') alone (EVM length 2) to isolate the empty-string rule.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode==abi.encodePacked collapse generalizes beyond unsigned integer tuples to signed integer tuples (int8/int16/int256 mixed with uint64, both negative and positive-intermediate values, observed in crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-static-p2-signed), so solang's abi.encode is now confirmed non-canonical for every integer-tuple composition tested; the remaining open question is whether NON-INTEGER statics (address, bool, bytesNN) also collapse (polkadot encoded digest == packed digest, diverging from EVM's canonical 96/64-byte encodings) or whether abi.encode is canonical for them, which would make the collapse integer-specific rather than universal for static argument lists.

evidence.note: No direct evidence yet (this probe used only integer args); h10's confirmation establishes the collapse for all-static integer tuples at four value sets, making the natural generalization question whether non-integer statics (address, bool, bytesNN) share the same non-canonical abi.encode behavior. Hash correctness (h7) means digest comparison is a valid byte-equality oracle.

Signed-tuple steps show polkadot encoded==packed for all three hash functions on both arg sets, extending h10's value-independent collapse from unsigned to signed integer tuples; no address/bool/bytesNN argument was present, so h12's core non-integer question remains unresolved.

Non-integer static tuple (address,bool,bytes4): on polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x6a70c173... (step 0) and 0xe0dc776e... (step 1), packedSha==encodedSha==0xadd6bce1... / 0x1f72da2d..., while EVM keeps all four digests distinct (packed 0x3e9fd8ed.../0x383ec8f3... vs encoded 0x4ff19c63.../0x5492cbaf...). The abi.encode==abi.encodePacked collapse therefore generalizes beyond integer tuples to address/bool/bytesNN compositions, answering h12's core question: solang's abi.encode is non-canonical for static argument lists regardless of whether the statics are integers.

hypotheses.next_probe: Static non-integer probe: store/emit keccak256 of abi.encodePacked(addr,true,0xdeadbeef) and abi.encode(addr,true,0xdeadbeef) plus abi.encode(true,false) on both chains (EVM encode lengths 96 and 64; packed lengths 25 and 2). If polkadot encoded==packed digests, the collapse generalizes to all static types; if polkadot encoded digest matches EVM's canonical encoding, the collapse is integer-tuple-specific.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked handles empty and one-char dynamic string tails correctly (lengths and keccak digests bit-identical to EVM) when the static head consists of small uniform types (four uint8s); therefore the packed divergence seen in crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-static-p2-dyn-tail step 1 ((1,2,3,4,'') with a mixed uint8/uint16/uint64/uint256 head) must be conditioned on the static head containing wide/multi-byte integer types rather than on the empty string itself — e.g., solang may mis-pack the static head (widths/padding) only in certain type compositions, with the 'x' case in the same probe accidentally matching.

evidence.note: Clean PASS on all six storage values (three lengths, three digests) with an all-uint8 static head plus ''/'x'/alone dynamic args. Combined with h7's hash correctness, this proves byte-identical packed output on both chains for this composition, so the earlier empty-string packed divergence must depend on the wider static-head types used in p2-dyn-tail.

Wide multi-byte static head with INTERMEDIATE values diverges on the packed side even with no dynamic argument at all: at a=170 EVM packedKeccak=0xd4fe8d5c... vs polkadot 0x3ed8459b...; at a=128 EVM 0xe98d2764... vs polkadot 0x41b8ea53... (all other args 48879, 81985529216486895, 2e19 identical). Since h7 established the hash primitives are correct, solang's packed bytes for this composition differ from EVM's, strengthening the conclusion that the p2-dyn-tail step-1 divergence was caused by the wide static head rather than the empty string. Notably the same arg sets matched across chains at all-max/all-zero (h9/h10), so the divergence appears only for non-boundary byte patterns.

hypotheses.next_probe: Length+digest probe on both chains: abi.encodePacked(uint8(1),uint16(2),uint64(3),uint256(4),"").length (EVM expects 1+2+8+32+0=43) and abi.encodePacked(uint8(1),uint16(2),uint64(3),uint256(4),"x").length (EVM 44), plus keccak256 of both. If the empty-string length diverges while 'x' matches, the bug is an empty-tail interaction with the wide head; if both match, the p2-dyn-tail divergence needs re-triage (possibly a probe artifact).

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked/abi.encode emit multi-byte integers in little-endian (or otherwise byte-order-corrupted) byte order rather than EVM's big-endian: packed digests match EVM bit-for-bit exactly when integer bytes are endian-invariant (all-max, all-zero, single-byte uint8 heads, and dynamic content like 'hi'/0x1234 which matched in h7/h8) but diverge for intermediate values with asymmetric bytes, e.g. (170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) where EVM packedKeccak=0xd4fe8d5c... vs solang 0x3ed8459b... and EVM packedKeccak=0xe98d2764... vs solang 0x41b8ea53... for a=128. This single rule unifies every prior observation: h9/h10 boundary matches, h7 mixed-type matches, h8 step-1 (uint16(2),uint64(3),uint256(4) head) divergence, and h13's empty-string false lead.

evidence.note: Two intermediate value sets with a mixed uint8/uint16/uint64/uint256 head show polkadot packedKeccak != EVM packedKeccak (0x3ed8459b... vs 0xd4fe8d5c... at a=170; 0x41b8ea53... vs 0xe98d2764... at a=128) while polkadot packed==encoded (collapse) and the polkadot a=170 value exactly reproduces the original probe's 0x3ed8459b... (determinism re-confirmed). The a=128 polkadot value 0x41b8ea53... exactly reproduces the p2 probe's a=128 polkadot value. All prior cross-chain packed matches occurred only at endian-invariant inputs, implicating byte order in multi-byte integer packing.

Both steps reproduce p2-p0's digests exactly (polkadot 0x41b8ea53... at a=128, 0x3ed8459b... at a=170; EVM 0xe98d2764... and 0xd4fe8d5c...), re-confirming determinism. Critically, ripemd160 now also diverges on the packed side at these intermediate values (EVM 0x06dbdf4e... vs polkadot 0x2df0cae9... at a=128; 0xf8db8c5a... vs 0x7933883e... at a=170), so the intermediate-value divergence spans all three hash functions while boundary/all-zero/single-byte-head inputs matched — exactly the signature of a byte-order-corrupted multi-byte integer encoder upstream of the hash, as h14 states. The packed==encode collapse persists on polkadot in both steps, so the corruption is shared by both encoding paths.

hypotheses.next_probe: Minimal width-isolated probe: store keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint16(0x1234))), keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint64(0x0123456789abcdef))), and keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint32(0xdeadbeef))) on both chains (each a single multi-byte integer, no other args). EVM expects digests of the big-endian byte sequences 0x1234, 0x0123456789abcdef, 0xdeadbeef; if solang emits little-endian the digests will differ and exactly pin the byte-order reversal per width. Also include abi.encode(uint16(0x1234)) length: EVM=32, solang predicted=2 if the collapse also holds for single non-256-bit statics.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked/abi.encode emit multi-byte integers in little-endian (or otherwise byte-order-corrupted) byte order relative to EVM's big-endian, and the corruption spans every multi-byte integer slot: it was previously shown for uint8/uint16 heads (h14, varying a), and now the uint64 slot itself — with a completely fresh endian-asymmetric value 0x0123456789abcdee (c=81985529216486894, one less than the standard test constant) — produces brand-new divergent packed digests on all three hash functions (polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xf6c1520d..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x4791a140..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x535d176c... vs EVM packed 0xa520a2e6.../0x8baeac01.../0x0e6aa3f3...), with the packed==encode collapse intact. Refuted if any single-integer probe digest matches the big-endian preimage or neither endianness's digest.

evidence.note: All three hash functions diverge on packed bytes at intermediate (endian-asymmetric) values while matching at endian-invariant inputs across the campaign; this is the deduced precondition for asserting a byte-order mechanism, but direction and per-width behavior are not yet directly observed, so the mechanism remains to be pinned by single-integer probes.

Step 0 varies only c to 81985529216486894 (0x0123456789abcdee), a previously unobserved endian-asymmetric byte pattern: all three polkadot packed digests are fresh (0xf6c1520d.../0x4791a140.../0x535d176c...) and duplicated (packed==encoded, collapse holds), while all three EVM packed digests (0xa520a2e6.../0x8baeac01.../0x0e6aa3f3...) are distinct from both polkadot values and from EVM's own encoded values. Step 1 with the canonical (170,48879,...,895,2e19) tuple reproduces every prior deployment's polkadot digests exactly (0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e..., collapsed) and EVM's distinct packed values (0xd4fe8d5c.../0x6684c3b4.../0xf8db8c5a...), re-confirming determinism. The divergence is now shown to be driven by the uint64 slot's byte content as well, consistent with per-slot little-endian reversal.

The exact width-isolated probe h15 specified ran: single-argument keccak256(abi.encodePacked(x)) and keccak256(abi.encode(x)) for uint16(4660), uint32(3735928559), uint64(81985529216486895). On polkadot k16==e16==0x94619a1e..., k32==e32==0xc872ba77..., k64==e64==0xbe3a6c36...: the packed==encode collapse holds even for single non-256-bit statics (abi.encode(uint16) emits 2 bytes, not 32), and all three widths diverge from EVM (EVM keeps packed/encoded distinct, 0x56570de2.../0xe321d900..., 0xd4fd4e18.../0x2cefe4e5..., 0x0c3d7239.../0x7b276d82...). The corruption is per-slot: no tuple interaction is needed, exactly as h15's per-slot little-endian mechanism predicts. EVM k16 shares the 18-byte prefix 0x56570de287d73cd1cb6092bb8f with the known keccak256(0x1234) reference, corroborating big-endian 0x1234 as EVM's preimage. Direction of reversal still pending offline digest comparison (see h20).

hypotheses.next_probe: Single-integer width probe on both chains: store keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint16(0x1234))), keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint32(0xdeadbeef))), keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint64(0x0123456789abcdef))) and abi.encodePacked(...).length for each; compare against precomputed digests of both big-endian and little-endian preimages to pin the reversal per width.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode/abi.encodePacked byte output is stable across independent deployments and probe runs: the intermediate arg sets (170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) and (128,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) now reproduce bit-identical polkadot digests (packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x3ed8459b... and 0x41b8ea53... respectively; ripemd160 0x7933883e... and 0x2df0cae9...) in a third fresh contract instance, while EVM's six digests remain distinct and its packed side keeps matching nothing on polkadot. The encoding divergence is therefore a deterministic, compiler-emitted property (consistent with a fixed byte-order bug in the SCALE-to-ABI encoder), not runtime or environment nondeterminism — this upgrades the triage confidence of h14/h15's bug_candidate without needing further determinism probes.

evidence.note: Third exact reproduction: step 0 (a=170) yields polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x3ed8459b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xc571f7b8..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x7933883e...; step 1 (a=128) yields 0x41b8ea53.../0x06b5c7a7.../0x2df0cae9... — all identical to the original probe, p2-p0, and p2-p1 values, while EVM's six digests are all distinct per step and its packed digests (0xd4fe8d5c.../0xe98d2764... keccak, 0x6684c3b4.../0x759ec46c... sha, 0xf8db8c5a.../0x06dbdf4e... ripemd) match nothing on polkadot. Fresh deployment, identical bytes out: deterministic compiler-side encoding divergence.

A fourth independent run again reproduces every prior digest exactly: step 0 (all-max) yields polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x7cfb035b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x19462e5b..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x2ad23945... with the packed side matching EVM bit-for-bit and only the three encoded slots diverging; step 1 (all-zero) yields polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xdafb08ad..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x859732b9..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0xd93a7bc1..., same cross-chain pattern. These boundary digests were already stable across boundary-args and p2-boundary-max; reproducing them again in a fresh deployment confirms the encoding divergence is a deterministic compiler-emitted property (consistent with a fixed byte-order bug in the SCALE-to-ABI encoder), not runtime nondeterminism.

hypotheses.next_probe: Single-integer width probe (same as h15): store keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint16(0x1234))), keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint32(0xdeadbeef))), keccak256(abi.encodePacked(uint64(0x0123456789abcdef))) on both chains and compare against precomputed big-endian vs little-endian digests to pin the reversal direction per width.

hypotheses.statement: solang's non-canonical abi.encode/abi.encodePacked output is stateless and history-independent: the digests emitted for a given argument tuple depend only on the current inputs, not on prior set() calls to the same contract instance. Within this probe one instance was first set to (0,0,0,0) then overwritten with (170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19), and both steps' polkadot digests exactly reproduce every prior fresh-deployment value (0xdafb08ad... for all-zero, 0x3ed8459b... for intermediate), with no cross-contamination of storage. The encoding divergence is therefore a pure function of args (compiler-emitted encoding bug), not instance-state-dependent behavior.

evidence.note: Step 0 (all-zero) yields polkadot 0xdafb08ad.../0x859732b9.../0xd93a7bc1... (packed==encoded, matching EVM packed) and step 1 (intermediate) yields 0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e... (packed==encoded) — both bit-identical to all prior deployments' polkadot values, while polkadot step-1 storage shows only 3 unique digests (each duplicated), proving no residue from step 0 influenced step 1.

One instance received set() twice with identical args (128,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) plus a sentinel write each call; both steps' polkadot events are bit-identical (packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x41b8ea53... both times) and reproduce every prior deployment's a=128 polkadot value, while EVM's six digests stay distinct with packedKeccak 0xe98d2764... matching prior EVM packed values. Repeated same-instance state writes (including a new uint128 sentinel slot mutated each call) leave the emitted digests a pure function of args, confirming history/state-independence of the encoding divergence.

hypotheses.next_probe: Within one instance call set(A), set(B), set(A) with A=(170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) and B=(0,0,0,0), querying all six getters after each call: confirmation requires the third call's polkadot digests to exactly reproduce the first call's (0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e...) and EVM's likewise, proving history-independence; the signed probe's two sequential overwrites are consistent with but do not by themselves prove it.

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encode==abi.encodePacked collapse and the endianness-corrupted multi-byte integer encoding both extend to SIGNED integer types: for (int8(-1), int16(-2), uint64, int256(-1)) and (int8(-128), int16(32767), uint64(0), int256(1)), polkadot emits packedKeccak==encodedKeccak (0xeedf86a2... and 0x19937ca1...), packedSha==encodedSha, packedRipemd==encodedRipemd, while EVM keeps all six digests distinct; and the packed digests diverge from EVM exactly when the tuple contains endian-asymmetric multi-byte values (int16(-2)=0xfffe, int16(32767)=0x7fff), matching h14's endianness signature including for negative two's-complement bytes.

evidence.note: Step 0 (-1,-2,81985529216486895,-1): polkadot shows all six slots in duplicated pairs (packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xeedf86a2..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xffd20cf9..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x1d0896ca...) while EVM's six digests are distinct (packedKeccak 0x5b58a4e0..., packedSha 0x732f155f...); polkadot packed side matches nothing on EVM. Step 1 (-128,32767,0,1): same pattern (polkadot 0x19937ca1.../0xe81efd77.../0xd4e22789... duplicated pairs; EVM six distinct values). Both steps contain endian-asymmetric int16 bytes (0xfffe, 0x7fff) and diverge on the packed side, consistent with h14/h15's byte-order mechanism now covering signed types; the packed==encode collapse also holds for signed tuples.

Exact reproduction of crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-static-p2-signed in a fresh deployment: step 0 (-1,-2,81985529216486895,-1) again yields polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0xeedf86a2..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xffd20cf9..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x1d0896ca..., and step 1 (-128,32767,0,1) again yields 0x19937ca1.../0xe81efd77.../0xd4e22789... (all collapsed pairs), while EVM keeps six distinct digests per step (step 0 packedKeccak 0x5b58a4e0..., step 1 packedKeccak 0x37628ab8...). Both signed steps contain endian-asymmetric int16 bytes (0xfffe, 0x7fff) and diverge on the packed side, confirming the collapse and the endianness signature extend to signed integer tuples; bit-exact reproduction across deployments also extends h16/h17's determinism/statelessness findings to signed types.

hypotheses.next_probe: Single signed-integer width probe on both chains: store keccak256(abi.encodePacked(int16(-2))) and keccak256(abi.encodePacked(int16(32767))) and compare against precomputed digests of big-endian (0xfffe / 0x7fff) vs little-endian (0xfeff / 0xff7f) preimages; if solang matches the little-endian digests, signed ints share the same reversal as unsigned; also check abi.encode(int8(-1)).length (EVM=32) to see whether the collapse pads single-byte signed statics.

hypotheses.statement: solang's non-canonical abi.encode/abi.encodePacked digests are independent of contract storage layout: inserting a new uint128 storage variable (sentinel) ahead of all six hash slots shifts every slot by one yet the a=128 polkadot digests exactly reproduce the unshifted probes' values (0x41b8ea53.../0x06b5c7a7.../0x2df0cae9..., packed==encoded), so the byte-order/packing bug lives purely in the abi-encode codegen, not in storage serialization or slot addressing. Additionally the sentinel arithmetic itself agrees cross-chain: sentinel = uint128(48879)+1 = 48880 appears in both EVM and polkadot storage sets, so the layout shift introduced no new divergence in the non-hash state path.

evidence.note: With sentinel prepended, polkadot step digests (0x41b8ea53.../0x06b5c7a7.../0x2df0cae9..., all packed==encoded) are byte-identical to the unshifted p2/p2-p0/p2-p1/p2-p2 polkadot values for the same args, and the sentinel value 48880 is present in both chains' storage multisets; the only divergences are the six hash slots themselves, reproduced exactly as before.

Declaring the six hash storage variables in a different order (ripemd slots first instead of keccak first) yields polkadot digests bit-identical to every prior unshifted deployment for both arg sets: a=170 gives packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x3ed8459b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xc571f7b8..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x7933883e...; a=128 gives 0x41b8ea53.../0x06b5c7a7.../0x2df0cae9..., while EVM's six distinct digests (packed 0xd4fe8d5c.../0x6684c3b4.../0xf8db8c5a..., encoded 0x4cf8beb6.../0x46b8c5e6.../0x51de5651...) also reproduce exactly. Declaration order of the storage slots leaves the emitted digests a pure function of args, confirming the encoding divergence is entirely in abi-encode codegen and independent of storage layout/ordering.

hypotheses.next_probe: Cross-check layout independence with a DECODED comparison rather than multiset: declare the hash vars in a different declaration ORDER (e.g., ripemd slots before keccak slots) and re-run the a=170 arg set; if polkadot digests still reproduce 0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e... exactly, layout independence is fully pinned. Alternatively declare a dynamic-length bytes state variable appended after the hash slots to test whether dynamic storage (keccak-slot hashing in the layout) perturbs solang's encoder output.

hypotheses.statement: solang's multi-byte integer encoding is byte-order-reversed (little-endian) rather than merely 'different': the polkadot digests from the width-isolated probe should equal keccak256 of the little-endian preimages — k16 == keccak256(0x3412) (vs EVM's keccak256(0x1234)), k32 == keccak256(0xefbeadde) for 0xdeadbeef, k64 == keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) for 0x0123456789abcdef — since all prior cross-chain matches occurred only at endian-invariant inputs and every endian-asymmetric input diverged. Refuted if the stored polkadot values 0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36... match the big-endian digests instead, or neither endianness.

evidence.note: Provides the three clean single-width polkadot digests (0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36...) against which the little-endian hypothesis can be checked with no confounding tuple composition; EVM side confirmed big-endian via prefix match to the known keccak256(0x1234) value.

Indirect corroboration of the little-endian mechanism: the near-max arg set produces packed bytes whose digests (0x114a545d... keccak) diverge from EVM despite being only one below the all-max set that matched EVM exactly (0x7cfb035b...) — a magnitude-based bug would predict near-max to match all-max closely, but a per-slot byte-reversal predicts exactly this: flipping the low byte from 0xff to 0xfe makes the slot asymmetric (0xfffe vs reversed 0xfeff) and the digest diverges. No direction pinned yet; the offline check against 0x94619a1e.../0xc872ba77.../0xbe3a6c36... remains the decisive step.

hypotheses.next_probe: Cheapest: pure offline check — compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) and string-compare against the stored polkadot values 0x94619a1ed333..., 0xc872ba77ace3..., 0xbe3a6c360d4a...; no new deployment needed. If on-chain evidence is wanted instead, expose a view returning abi.encodePacked(uint16(0x1234)) as raw bytes (EVM returns 0x1234; little-endian solang predicted 0x3412).

hypotheses.statement: solang's abi.encodePacked (the packed path itself, not just the abi.encode collapse) may be broken for address/bool/bytes4 statics: in this probe the polkadot packed digests (0x6a70c173..., 0xe0dc776e...) matched nothing on EVM, whereas prior probes showed integer-only and dynamic-containing packed paths often matching EVM bit-for-bit. The packed mismatch here is NOT yet attributable to an encoding bug because $alice/$bob resolve to different chain-specific addresses, so the packed input bytes provably differ across chains; the divergence would persist even if solang packed address/bool/bytes4 correctly. Refuted if a same-literal-address probe produces bit-identical packed digests across chains.

evidence.note: Step 0 ($alice,true,0xdeadbeef) and step 1 ($bob,false,0x00000000) both show polkadot packed==encoded pairs diverging from all four distinct EVM digests; storage count mode shows 4 nonzero entries on both chains with each polkadot value duplicated (collapse visible in raw storage). Because the address argument differs per chain by construction, the packed-side gap is confounded and cannot be assigned to solang's encoder without a constant-address control.

hypotheses.next_probe: Replace the address-literal design (now known to be solang-uncompilable) with a parameter-passed address: set(address a) storing packedKeccak=keccak256(abi.encodePacked(a,true,bytes4(0xdeadbeef))), pSha, and eKeccak, called on both chains with the same 20-byte value (e.g. 0x0000...0001 passed as a hex argument, avoiding any literal in source). If packed digests then match EVM bit-for-bit, solang's packed encoding of address/bool/bytesNN is correct and only abi.encode collapses; if they diverge, the non-canonical packing extends to these types.

hypotheses.statement: solang rejects bare 20-byte hexadecimal address literals (e.g. address constant A = 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD) at compile time with 'ethereum address literal ... not supported on target Polkadot', while solc accepts them; this is a pure compile-time asymmetry analogous to h1's ecrecover case, meaning no address-typed packed/encoded runtime comparison can use address literals on the solang side and any h21-style constant-address control must obtain the address by a non-literal construction (cast, parameter, or msg.sender).

evidence.note: solc compiled and ran; solang failed at line 3 with 'ethereum address literal 0x000000000000000000000000000000000000dEaD not supported on target Polkadot' — the entire probe (constant-address packed/encoded digest comparison) was unobservable, so h21's planned control was blocked by a toolchain gate before any runtime bytes could be compared.

hypotheses.statement: solang's non-canonical abi.encode/abi.encodePacked behavior is now invariant under every perturbation tested: extra prepended sentinel slot (h19), declaration-order reorder (h19), repeated same-instance overwrites (h17), fresh deployments (h16), and now tx-sender variation plus emit-statement reordering (p2-emit-swap) — the emitted digests are a pure function of the abi-encode arguments in all cases, so the bug is conclusively localized to solang's ABI-encode codegen emitting per-slot byte-order-corrupted integers with no abi.encode/abi.encodePacked distinction for static tuples; the only remaining unproven sub-claim is the reversal DIRECTION itself (h20), decidable by an offline digest comparison against the stored single-width values 0x94619a1e.../0xc872ba77.../0xbe3a6c36....

evidence.note: Sender variation (bob vs alice) and swapped emit order left all digests bit-identical to every prior a=128 deployment on both chains, adding sender/origin-independence and event-order-independence to the list of invariance checks the encoding bug survives; the divergence signature (polkadot collapsed pairs vs EVM six distinct values) is unchanged.

Another fresh deployment with mixed senders (deployer then alice) and a novel combined arg set reproduces every prior digest bit-for-bit: step 0 (170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) yields polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x3ed8459b..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xc571f7b8..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x7933883e... (exact original-probe values), while EVM reproduces its six distinct digests (packedKeccak 0xd4fe8d5c..., encodedKeccak 0x4cf8beb6...). The encoding divergence survives sender alternation plus an unobserved arg combination with zero drift, further cementing that emitted digests are a pure function of abi-encode arguments. Only the h20 offline direction check remains.

hypotheses.next_probe: Pure offline check: compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) (little-endian preimages of 0x1234, 0xdeadbeef, 0x0123456789abcdef) and compare against the stored polkadot digests from crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-single-int-width; matching confirms h20 and completes the endianness proof chain with no new deployment.

hypotheses.statement: solang's packed/encoded digest divergence is governed by the endian-symmetry of the argument bytes, not their magnitude: near-max asymmetric values (254=0xfe, 65534=0xfffe, 2^64-2, 2^256-2) diverge from EVM on all three packed digests exactly like interior intermediate values, while all-max (all 0xff) and all-zero (endian-invariant) matched EVM bit-for-bit. This closes the apparent gap between h9/h10's boundary matches and h14/h15's intermediate divergences: the single governing variable is whether the big-endian byte pattern is palindromic under reversal. The packed==encode collapse also holds at near-max (packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x114a545d..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xe8da6eab..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x4aeae810...), and all polkadot slots come in duplicated pairs while EVM keeps six distinct values.

evidence.note: Args one below max in every slot (254, 65534, 2^64-2, 2^256-2): EVM packedKeccak=0x9ace0efc..., packedSha=0x8085c72c..., packedRipemd=0xb57b8f5b... vs polkadot 0x114a545d.../0xe8da6eab.../0x4aeae810... on the packed side, all three hash functions diverging, while polkadot shows packed==encoded collapse on all three and EVM keeps six distinct digests. Since near-max bytes (0xfe, 0xfffe, ...fffe) are endian-asymmetric, this behaves identically to interior intermediates and unlike all-max/all-zero, confirming magnitude is irrelevant and byte-pattern symmetry is the sole determinant.

Step 0 with a fresh endian-asymmetric value c=81985529216486896 (0x0123456789abcdf0, one above the canonical test constant) diverges from EVM on all three packed digests (EVM 0xf3309ea1.../0x7c22ef54.../0x1ca29356... vs polkadot 0x560cdd5c.../0x94c92466.../0x3c0deb0b...), while polkadot shows the packed==encode collapse on all three and EVM keeps six distinct values. Combined with step 1 (c=0x0123456789abcdee) exactly reproducing h15's polkadot values (0xf6c1520d.../0x4791a140.../0x535d176c...) and EVM's (0xa520a2e6.../0x8baeac01.../0x0e6aa3f3...) in a fresh deployment, this shows the divergence governed by endian-symmetry has no magnitude dead-zone: perturbing an asymmetric slot by +-1 still diverges, while exact boundary values (all-max/all-zero) match. Magnitude irrelevance and byte-pattern symmetry as the sole determinant are now established at max-adjacent, canonical-adjacent, and interior values.

hypotheses.next_probe: None needed for the symmetry rule; to pin the reversal direction, run the offline digest check from h20: compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) and compare against the stored single-width polkadot digests 0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36... from crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-single-int-width.

hypotheses.statement: solang's non-canonical abi.encode/abi.encodePacked digests are sender-independent: calling set() twice with identical args (128,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) from two different senders (bob then alice) yields bit-identical polkadot digests (packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x41b8ea53..., packedSha==encodedSha==0x06b5c7a7..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x2df0cae9...) reproducing every prior deployment, and the reordered emit statements (HashRipemd before Hash32) produce the same event sequence on both chains — so the encoding divergence is a pure function of the abi-encode arguments, with no dependence on tx sender/origin or emit-statement ordering.

evidence.note: Steps 0 (bob) and 1 (alice) with identical args produce bit-identical events and storage on each chain: polkadot emits collapsed pairs 0x41b8ea53.../0x06b5c7a7.../0x2df0cae9... in both steps (exactly reproducing all prior a=128 deployments), while EVM emits six distinct values (packedKeccak 0xe98d2764..., encodedKeccak 0xac8aaf8f..., packedSha 0x759ec46c..., encodedSha 0x819941e8..., packedRipemd 0x06dbdf4e..., encodedRipemd 0x25fd46e9...) also stable across both steps. The only divergence is the known value gap; sender identity and swapped emit order introduced no new asymmetry.

Sender alternation plus a novel arg combination leaves all digests a pure function of args: step 0 (128,48879,81985529216486894,2e19) called by alice reproduces h15/p2-p1-p0's values bit-for-bit on both chains (polkadot collapsed pairs 0xf6c1520d.../0x4791a140.../0x535d176c...; EVM six distinct with packed 0xa520a2e6.../0x8baeac01.../0x0e6aa3f3...), and step 1 (170,48879,...,2e19) called by deployer reproduces the original probe's polkadot values (0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e... collapsed) and EVM's (packed 0xd4fe8d5c.../0x6684c3b4.../0xf8db8c5a..., encoded 0x4cf8beb6.../0x46b8c5e6.../0x51de5651...) exactly. The (a=128, c=...ee) combination was never deployed before, yet its digests match what determinism predicts from the per-slot reversal model; sender identity (alice vs deployer) and call order introduce zero drift. h25's sender/origin-independence and emit-order-independence claims are both directly supported, and the only divergence is the known encoding gap.

To finish the mechanism, run the h20 offline check: compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) and compare against stored polkadot digests 0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36... from crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-single-int-width.

hypotheses.statement: h8's refuted 'empty string corrupts packed encoding' lead is fully closed: keccak256/sha256 digests of abi.encodePacked(1,2,3,4) reproduce the p2-dyn-tail step-1 digests bit-for-bit on both chains (EVM 0x6387eff5.../0x487f9503..., polkadot collapsed 0x56669b11.../0xd2a7182d...), so the empty string appended zero bytes on both sides and the earlier divergence was purely the wide static head's byte-order bug. The same step shows the smallest endian-asymmetric values (1,2,3,4) diverge on all three packed digests, extending h24's endian-symmetry rule to single-digit magnitudes with no low-end dead zone (only exact all-zero matched), while the nearmax step exactly reproduces h24's 0x114a545d.../0xe8da6eab.../0x4aeae810... collapsed values in a fresh deployment with deployer/alice sender alternation. Additionally, widening the mutated slot from uint8 to uint16 leaves the signature unchanged: a=256 (uint16 0x0100, a minimally asymmetric 2-byte pattern) diverges from EVM on all three packed digests in a fresh deployment with sender alternation (polkadot collapsed pairs 0x4799ffcd.../0x7ffa6668.../0x059928e4... vs EVM distinct packed 0xa053277f.../0xed7b55dd.../0xe88c2030...), and a step with the endian-invariant slot a=65535 (0xffff) still diverges because the b/c/d slots remain asymmetric — so per-slot byte-pattern symmetry, not slot width or position, is the sole determinant, with no width-based escape from the endianness rule.

evidence.note: Step 0 (254,65534,2^64-2,2^256-2) exactly reproduces h24's nearmax values: polkadot packedKeccak==encodedKeccak==0x114a545d..., packedSha==encodedSha==0xe8da6eab..., packedRipemd==encodedRipemd==0x4aeae810...; EVM six distinct with packed 0x9ace0efc.../0x8085c72c.../0xb57b8f5b.... Step 1 (1,2,3,4) reproduces p2-dyn-tail step-1 digests bit-for-bit on both chains (EVM packed 0x6387eff5.../0x487f9503.../0x2e10804d...; polkadot collapsed 0x56669b11.../0xd2a7182d.../0x60544c38...), proving '' appended zero bytes and the empty-string lead was a head-encoding artifact; tiny asymmetric values diverge on the packed side, and sender alternation (deployer/alice) plus fresh deployment introduce zero drift.

The a slot was widened from uint8 to uint16. Step 0 (a=65535=0xffff, endian-invariant slot) still diverges from EVM on all three packed digests (EVM packedKeccak 0xd760a195.../packedSha 0x9ea67954.../packedRipemd 0xb6cb328b... vs polkadot collapsed 0x5bcfbac1.../0x490e5cb2.../0x5ff98445...) because b/c/d remain asymmetric, while polkadot shows packed==encode collapse on all three and EVM keeps six distinct values. Step 1 (a=256=0x0100, minimally asymmetric 2-byte pattern, c=0x0123456789abcdee) diverges on all three packed digests (EVM 0xa053277f.../0xed7b55dd.../0xe88c2030... vs polkadot collapsed 0x4799ffcd.../0x7ffa6668.../0x059928e4...) in a fresh deployment with deployer/alice sender alternation, exactly as the per-slot little-endian model predicts. All getter return-value mismatches mirror the event digests. No width- or position-based escape from the endian-symmetry rule; the only unconfirmed sub-claim remains the reversal direction (h20 offline check).

Both steps behave exactly as the per-slot endian-symmetry rule predicts with a uint16 a slot. Step 0 (a=256=0x0100 minimally asymmetric, b=48879=0xbeef, c=0x0123456789abcdef, d=2e19) diverges from EVM on all three packed digests (EVM packedKeccak 0x4f70cc59.../packedSha 0xa61ca72c.../packedRipemd 0x56e69fc0... vs polkadot collapsed pairs 0x7dc09a63.../0x08083032.../0x8e9301dc...). Step 1 (a=65535=0xffff endian-invariant slot, but b=0xfffe, c=0x0123456789abcdee, d=1 asymmetric) still diverges on all three packed digests (EVM 0xdf3d4e67.../0x7eb9996a.../0x046f5f94... vs polkadot collapsed 0xdbbec2c7.../0x8acb95c2.../0xd7b9a0dd...), while all six getter return mismatches mirror the events and polkadot shows packed==encode collapse on all three hash functions in both steps. A single asymmetric byte in d (value 1) does not rescue the encoding; slot width (uint16 head), slot position, magnitude, and sender alternation (deployer/alice) all introduce no escape from the rule. The only unconfirmed sub-claim remains the reversal direction (h20 offline check).

hypotheses.next_probe: Run the decisive h20 offline check: compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) and compare against the stored polkadot single-width digests 0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36... from crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-single-int-width; also predictively compute keccak256 of the per-slot little-endian packed preimage of (1,2,3,4) (43 bytes: 01 02 0002 0000000000000003 00000000000000000000000000000004 with each multi-byte slot reversed) and check it equals the observed polkadot 0x56669b11756c9969e56c5d9b8a51327924908026089daf21568748afd1e6a867. Delete-style probes are now known to be oracle-artifact-prone (h27) and add nothing.

hypotheses.statement: h27: solang's `delete` on a bytes32/bytes20 storage slot has the same observable semantics as solc's — after set(170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19) then resetPackedKeccak() (delete packedKeccak), the getPackedKeccak query produced NO return mismatch, i.e. both chains agreed on the post-delete value (consistent with zero on both). The step-1 STORAGE_MISMATCH is an oracle artifact, not a semantic divergence: polkadot's nonzero count drops 6->5 because its packed==encoded collapse stores duplicate values, so deleting one keccak slot removes one copy of the shared value from the multiset, whereas EVM's six distinct values make count-mode comparisons structurally asymmetric after any delete. Notably the EVM step-1 snapshot still lists six nonzero entries identical to step 0, contradicting its own getter result (which matched polkadot), so the count-mode storage capture appears stale/misattributed at that step and should not be trusted for delete-style probes; the raw getter evidence is the reliable channel.

evidence.note: Step 0 re-reproduces the canonical a=170 divergence exactly (polkadot collapsed pairs 0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e...; EVM six distinct 0xd4fe8d5c.../0x4cf8beb6.../0x6684c3b4.../0x46b8c5e6.../0xf8db8c5a.../0x51de5651...) — another determinism datapoint subsumed by h16/h23. Step 1 (delete packedKeccak): polkadot nonzero_entries drops 6->5 with the duplicated keccak value appearing once instead of twice (the collapsed-pair counting artifact), while the EVM snapshot anomalously still shows 6 identical nonzero entries. Critically, step 2 getPackedKeccak is ABSENT from the divergence list — both chains returned the same post-delete value — so delete semantics agree and the step-1 storage mismatch is an oracle artifact (stale/duplicated EVM capture plus duplicate-pair count sensitivity), not a toolchain behavioral divergence.

hypotheses.next_probe: Delete-restore probe with decoded comparison only: set(170,48879,81985529216486895,2e19), delete packedKeccak, query all six getters (packedKeccak expected 0 on both), then set() the same args again and confirm all six polkadot digests reproduce 0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e... (collapsed pairs) and EVM its six distinct values — pinning that delete+restore leaves the encoding bug a pure function of args and that the storage-count mismatch is purely the duplicate-pair counting artifact. Avoid storage count mode; compare getter return values only.

hypotheses.statement: solang's encoding divergence is invariant under SIMULTANEOUS combined layout perturbations: declaring a uint32 sentinel slot AND reordering the six hash storage declarations in the same contract (plus sender alternation via charlie/alice) still yields bit-identical polkadot digests for both arg sets — a=170 reproduces 0x3ed8459b.../0xc571f7b8.../0x7933883e... and a=128,c=...ee reproduces 0xf6c1520d.../0x4791a140.../0x535d176c... (all collapsed pairs), while EVM reproduces its six distinct digests (0xd4fe8d5c.../0x4cf8beb6.../0x6684c3b4.../0x46b8c5e6.../0xf8db8c5a.../0x51de5651... and 0xa520a2e6.../0x87b1a0c1.../0x8baeac01.../0xc335cbf8.../0x0e6aa3f3.../0xfdad1a83...). The two perturbations do not interact, and the sentinel arithmetic itself (uint32(48879)+7=48886) appears in both chains' storage multisets, so widening sentinel from uint128 to uint32 with a different offset (+7 vs +1) introduces no new divergence. This closes the perturbation-interaction question h19/h23 left open (they tested each perturbation only in isolation).

evidence.note: Combined field reorder + uint32 sentinel (b+7=48886, present on both chains) + charlie/alice sender alternation reproduced every prior digest bit-for-bit on both chains in a fresh deployment (step 0 = canonical a=170 values; step 1 = h15 c-varied values), with getter return mismatches exactly mirroring the event digests; no interaction effect between the two layout perturbations and no new divergence from the changed sentinel type/offset.

hypotheses.next_probe: No perturbation probes remain useful (h27 showed delete-style probes are oracle-artifact-prone); the only decisive remaining step is the h20 offline check: compute keccak256(0x3412), keccak256(0xefbeadde), keccak256(0xefcdab8967452301) and compare against stored polkadot digests 0x94619a1e..., 0xc872ba77..., 0xbe3a6c36... from crypto-hash-packed-vs-encode-single-int-width to pin the little-endian reversal direction.
